novel_features.name: Morning triage
novel_features.description: See new members, unreplied posts, flagged content, form submissions, failed charges and cancellations since a time, read from the local mirror.
novel_features.rationale: Joins six synced resources locally, so one command replaces six quota-metered API calls.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run sync first: inbox reads only the local mirror, and an empty or missing mirror returns empty sections with exit 0, not an all-clear.

novel_features.name: Declarative structure apply
novel_features.description: Make Circle's space groups and spaces match a YAML file, with a plan printed before any write.
novel_features.rationale: Diffs the file against live Circle across two resource types and changes only what differs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to set up or change community structure repeatably; rerunning an applied file is a no-op.

novel_features.name: Course push
novel_features.description: Upload a course kept as module folders and markdown lessons to a Circle course space, new lessons as drafts.
novel_features.rationale: Creates or updates sections and lessons, uploads media, and fixes order in one idempotent pass using a local id map.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Prints the plan by default; add --yes to push. New lessons land as drafts, and lesson order is tracked in course.yaml because Circle's API does not expose it.

novel_features.name: Course pull
novel_features.description: Download a Circle course space into module folders with one file per lesson; lesson bodies stay as Circle's HTML and media is not downloaded.
novel_features.rationale: Rebuilds the section and lesson tree with ids in frontmatter, so course push round-trips without duplicates.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to back up a course or hand it to an agent to edit as files; files are numbered in creation order because Circle's API does not expose lesson order.

novel_features.name: Seat count
novel_features.description: Count paying members against a seat cap and list who paid.
novel_features.rationale: Deduplicates payers across subscriptions and charges from the local mirror, with no aggregation endpoint upstream.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to see how many founding seats are left; active, trialing and past-due subscriptions plus paid charges count as paid.

novel_features.name: Batch onboarding
novel_features.description: Add people to the community, their spaces, space groups and access groups, and tag them, without sending invite emails by default.
novel_features.rationale: Chains member, space group, access group and tag calls per person and skips people who already exist.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Prints the plan by default; --yes applies it. No invite email goes out unless you add --send together with --yes.

novel_features.name: Founding go/no-go
novel_features.description: Answer whether at least N people paid with GO or NO-GO and the count.
novel_features.rationale: Uses the seat computation and returns a typed exit code an agent can branch on.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for the launch decision. Branch on the verdict field: exit 2 is also used for usage errors. Trialing and past-due subscriptions count as paid.

novel_features.name: Recurring session scheduler
novel_features.description: Create the next Show & Tell events on a cadence by duplicating a template event.
novel_features.rationale: Circle's API has no recurring series; this duplicates and reschedules per date and skips dates already scheduled.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Prints the series plan by default; --yes creates the occurrences as quiet drafts and records them so reruns skip dates already scheduled.

novel_features.name: Session recap draft
novel_features.description: Pull a past session's RSVPed attendees and its live-room transcript into a markdown recap draft.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the event, its attendees and the matching live room transcript, which Circle does not link.
novel_features.why_it_matters: A transcript needs a live-room recording near the event time; otherwise the recap says none was found (transcript_found false). --post --yes saves it as a draft post.

narrative.headline: Run a Circle community from the terminal: spaces as files, courses as files, seat counts, and an offline mirror.
narrative.value_prop: Every Circle Admin API V2 endpoint, plus commands built for operators who run a paid community and a course on Circle. Declare spaces in a file and apply only the diff, keep a course as markdown folders, count founding seats, onboard members without invite emails, and triage what needs you from a local SQLite mirror.
narrative.auth_narrative: Circle admin tokens come from Circle admin > Developers > Tokens. Export the token as `CIRCLE_API_TOKEN`; the CLI sends it as `Authorization: Token <token>`. Admin API calls count against your plan's monthly request quota (5,000 to 250,000 a month by plan), so read from the local mirror after `sync` where you can.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the binary runs without calling Circle
Mirror spaces, members, posts and payments locally
See what needs you, read from the mirror

troubleshoots.fix: Check `CIRCLE_API_TOKEN` is an Admin API V2 token (V1 tokens do not work), then run `circle-pp-cli doctor`.
Circle allows 2,000 requests per 5 minutes per IP. Wait a few minutes, then rerun with `--rate-limit 2`.
Run `circle-pp-cli sync` once, then use `search`, `analytics`, `seats` and `inbox` (or the MCP `sql` tool), which read the local mirror.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs to set up or run a Circle community through the Admin API: create or update spaces from a file, push a course from markdown, onboard members, count paid seats, schedule recurring events, or triage new activity. It suits scripted and agent use where every write should be previewed first.
anti_triggers: Creating a paywall, price, or coupon: the Admin API has no create endpoint, use the Circle admin UI
Reading lesson completion or progress: the API only writes progress
Member-facing features in your own app: use Circle's Headless Member API
Sending DMs or announcement emails without a person approving them

recipes.title: Preview a structure change
recipes.explanation: Prints the create and update plan; add --apply to make the changes.

recipes.title: Push course edits as drafts
recipes.explanation: Prints which sections and lessons would be created or updated; re-run with --yes to push them as drafts.

recipes.title: Launch decision
recipes.explanation: Exit 0 means at least 10 people paid; exit 2 means not yet.

recipes.title: Narrow a member listing
recipes.explanation: Keeps only the fields an agent needs from a large member payload.

recipes.title: Declare spaces in a file
recipes.explanation: spaces.yaml lists space_groups and spaces (name, slug, group, type, privacy flags); without --apply it only prints the plan.
